title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Escalation, Integration, Health & QBR (2026-03-04)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines the standard playbook used by Redwood Inference Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE) and Support for enterprise onboarding, integration, incident/escalation handling, known issues & workarounds, and recurring health checks / QBR cadence. It is a canonical reference for cross-functional ownership, SLAs, and the step-by-step procedures used during the first 90 days and ongoing account operations.

Scope:
- Applies to all enterprise customers using Redwood hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers onboarding checklist, integration guide highlights, severity-based escalation paths, standard workarounds for common issues, health-check cadence, and QBR agenda.

Owner and Roles

- Primary owner: Customer Success (CS) — onboarding program (owner: Ava Chen)
- Escalation owner: Support Oncall & Escalations team (primary contact: support-oncall@redwood.com)
- Integration / technical lead: Solutions Engineering (SE) — contact: se-team@redwood.com
- Engineering escalation: Eng-SRE / Runtime teams (eng-sre@redwood.com)
- Legal / Contracts: finance-legal@redwood.com (for contract/SLA questions)

Onboarding checklist (90-day template)

1) Pre-kickoff (before day 0)
   - Verify contract & billing account: finance-legal sign-off and billing integration completed.
   - Create primary contact list (CSM, SE, engineering leads, security contact).
   - Provision initial credentials and access for test environment (API key, org/project ID, region).

2) Day 0 — Kickoff meeting (CSM + SE + Customer + Support)
   - Agenda: goals, timeline, success metrics (latency, availability, cost targets), data residency/security requirements, key integration points.
   - Outcomes: agreed milestones, communication channel (Slack/Teams + ticketing), demo app access.

3) Week 1 — Integration & smoke tests
   - SE to provide integration guide and sample code snippets (Node/Python curl).
   - Customer runs smoke tests: token limits, auth validation, sample generate/chat/embeddings flows.
   - Confirm telemetry ingestion: logs, usage metrics, and cost dashboards are visible to customer and CS.

4) Weeks 2-4 — Performance tuning & runbook handover
   - Tune batching/timeout/quantization recommendations (Redwood Optimize suggestions).
   - Validate SLOs for latency and throughput with representative workload.
   - Deliver runbook for day-2 ops (scaling, cache invalidation, key rotation).

5) Weeks 5-12 — Production rollout & QBR setup
   - Canary to partial, then full rollout per rollout policy.
   - Schedule first 30/60/90-day QBRs and define success metrics & evaluation prompt-sets.

Integration guide (high-level)

- Supported flows: text generation, chat (function calling), embeddings, reranking.
- Typical integration steps:
  1. Obtain API key and set environment variable: REDWOOD_API_KEY
  2. Set org/project and region headers in calls (example header: X-Redwood-Org: <org-id>)
  3. Start with low-rate smoke tests: 1-5 req/s, sequence length <= 256 for latency baseline.
  4. Gradually ramp and enable prefix caching & batching per SDK instructions.

Example curl snippet (replace values):

  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":64}'

Configuration table (recommended defaults)

| Setting | Recommended value | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Initial concurrency | 5-10 concurrent requests | Start conservatively for first week |
| Max sequence length | 256 tokens | Increase after latency baseline established |
| Batching window | 10-30 ms | Use Redwood Optimize suggestions |
| Cache TTL | 300s for prefixes | Depends on workload repeatability |

Escalation playbook (severity definitions & response targets)

- Severity levels and targets:
  - S1 (Critical): Production outage or sustained 50%+ degradation of serving capacity affecting all users. Response target: 15 minutes acknowledgement, 1 hour mitigation plan.
  - S2 (High): Partial outage or severe degradation for a subset of traffic (e.g., a single region or model). Response target: 30 minutes acknowledgement, 4 hour mitigation plan.
  - S3 (Medium): Functional impact with a known workaround (e.g., degraded latency for non-critical workflows). Response target: 4 business hours acknowledgement, 1-3 business day resolution target.
  - S4 (Low): General questions, feature requests, docs issues. Response target: 1-3 business days.

Escalation path:
1. Customer files ticket in Zendesk / Support portal (auto-creates Slack thread if enabled).
2. Tier 1 triage (Support): validate customer, reproduce issue, collect logs & request IDs, assign severity, and attempt immediate mitigation.
3. Tier 2 (SE / CS / Oncall): deep-dive reproduction, short-term workaround, coordinate customer communication.
4. Tier 3 (Eng-SRE / Runtime): code-level/infra fixes, root cause analysis.
5. Executive escalation: invoked when SLA breach or high-risk customer impact; notify CSM, Head of Support, Head of Eng.

Contact & escalation matrix (primary)

- Support portal: https://support.redwood.ai (primary intake)
- Email: support@redwood.ai (monitored 24x7)
- Oncall pager: support-oncall@redwood.com (page for S1 only)
- Escalation slack channel: #esc-redwood-prod (internal)
- SE technical contact: se-team@redwood.com
- Eng-SRE pager: eng-oncall@redwood.com

Ticket triage checklist (Tier 1)

1. Confirm customer identity and environment (hosted / dedicated / private).
2. Gather: request-id, timestamps, region, model name, SDK version, sample request/response, logs, and any rate-limit headers.
3. Attempt reproduction in a test org.
4. Classify severity, apply immediate mitigations (fallback to alternative model/region, increase concurrency limits, restart worker pool in Dedicated).
5. If no immediate fix should be available, escalate to Tier 2 within SLA window.

Known issues & workarounds (living list)

| ID | Symptom | Affected deployments | Workaround / Mitigation | ETA for fix | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|
| KI-2025-01 | KV cache growth causing OOM on long-running sessions | Dedicated GPU pools, on-prem | Rotate sessions every 12 hours; enable automatic KV trim in runtime config: "kv_trim_interval": 3600 | 2026-04-15 | eng-serving-runtime |
| KI-2025-10 | Token counting mismatch with downstream billing | Hosted API | Recompute usage with server-side token counter, apply credit offset; temporary billing override for affected customers | 2026-03-20 | finance-and-legal |
| KI-2026-03 | TLS renegotiation errors on older OpenSSL clients | Private deployments | Upgrade client OpenSSL 1.1.1+ or enable legacy-ciphers in proxy config as documented | 2026-05-01 | eng-infra |

- Process: CS maintains this living table in the doc; each row must include owner, ETA, and confidence level. When workaround is implemented, CS adds a customer-facing KB article.

Health checks & QBR materials

Recurring health checks (weekly):
- Weekly dashboard snapshot: token consumption, cost per 1000 tokens, p95/p99 latency, error-rate (%) by route/model, cache hit rate, and model fallback events.
- Actionable thresholds: error-rate > 0.5% sustained over 30m -> open incident; p99 latency increase > 2x baseline -> create performance triage ticket.

QBR template (30 / 60 / 90 / Quarterly):
- Attendees: CSM, Customer Engineering Lead, SE, Support Lead, Customer Product Manager.
- Agenda:
  1. Review objectives & success metrics (CSM)
  2. Production health snapshot (Support) — latency, errors, costs, anomalies
  3. Integration updates (SE) — new endpoints, SDK upgrades, upcoming migrations
  4. Optimization opportunities (Redwood Optimize) — batching, caching, quantization recommendations
  5. Roadmap & upcoming breaking changes (Product) — include migration windows and deprecation timelines
  6. Action items & owner assignment with due dates

Deliverables after QBR:
- QBR deck exported to customer folder and attached to ticket record.
- Action item tracker entry (owners and due dates) in CS project board.

Post-incident & regression triage

- After severity S1/S2 incidents: immediate incident review within 72 hours, full postmortem within 10 business days. Postmortem must include root cause, customer impact, remediation, and regression test to prevent recurrence.
- Regression gating: any model, SDK, or infra change that increases error-rate or latency for a verified customer workload must pass canary & automated regression suite before global rollout.

Communication templates

- Initial acknowledgement (S1 template):
  "We are aware of a production impact affecting <customer> in <region>. Support has acknowledged the issue and an investigation is underway. We will provide updates every 30 minutes until mitigation."

- Resolution update (S1/S2 template):
  "Issue mitigated at <time>. Root cause: <summary>. Impact: <scope>. Next steps: <fix ETA> and postmortem date."

Maintenance & planned downtime

- Any planned maintenance affecting production must be communicated at least 72 hours in advance for enterprise customers. Change record must include expected impact, rollback plan, and contact for escalation.

How to extend / modify this playbook

- Owners (CS) review this page quarterly and after any P0/P1 incident.
- Submit suggested edits via PR to the CS playbook repo and assign to the playbook owner for review.
